thread.title_full: Hermening formally launches bid for 7th Congressional District seat - NewsBreak

author: Shereen Siewert
title: Hermening formally launches bid for 7th Congressional District seat - NewsBreak
text:
By Shereen Siewert ,
11 hours ago WAUSAU — Republican Kevin Hermening formally launched his campaign Thursday for Wisconsin’s open 7th Congressional District seat, entering a crowded GOP primary with a message centered on deep local roots, decades of party involvement and frustration with Washington.
Hermening, a Marine veteran, small business owner and former chair of the Marathon County Republican Party, made his announcement at the Marathon County GOP headquarters in Wausau. The seat is opening after Rep. Tom Tiffany announced plans to run for governor in 2026.
“I’m not running to be somebody – I’m running to do something,” Hermening said. “This district deserves a representative who has lived here, worked here, and stood shoulder to shoulder with neighbors through both the good times and the hard times.”
Hermening has been active in Republican politics in north-central Wisconsin for more than 40 years. He has served as chair of the Marathon County Republican Party, was a member of the Mosinee School Board and has volunteered on numerous local and statewide campaigns. He also built and operated a local business in the district.
During his announcement speech, Hermening emphasized long-standing relationships across the region and framed his candidacy as an extension of that work.
“We’ve been in the trenches together. That builds a bond. And that bond is why I’m running,” he said.
Hermening, who was held hostage during the 1979 Iran hostage crisis while serving as a U.S. Marine, said those life experiences shaped his views on leadership and accountability.
“When you’ve seen the consequences of weak leadership, you understand why seriousness matters,” Hermening said. “I am prepared to serve from day one.”
He cited concerns about federal spending, national debt, border security and economic uncertainty as central motivations for his run.
“Families, seniors, veterans, farmers, and small businesses deserve better than what Washington has delivered,” Hermening said. “This seat is a serious responsibility. It requires judgment, steadiness, and a commitment to representing the people of this district.”
Hermening joins several Republicans seeking the nomination in the reliably conservative district, which spans much of northern and central Wisconsin. Among his opponents is Michael Alfonso , a Republican candidate who has received an endorsement from President Donald Trump.
Trump’s endorsement of Alfonso has drawn national attention to the race and sparked discussion among local Republicans about whether experience and long-standing ties to the district are crucial to the role.
Hermening addressed that dynamic indirectly during his remarks.
“When we don’t send neighbors we know and trust to the swamp in DC, that they don’t vote in our interests?” Hermening said. “Their money comes from out of state. Their values are from out of state. And their votes don’t represent the people of their state.”
Hermening also praised Tiffany, calling him “a great congressman,” and pointed to the district’s history of electing leaders with strong local connections.
The Republican primary is scheduled for Aug. 11, 2026. The winner will advance to the November general election in a district that has been held by Republicans for decades
“I love my home here in the 7th district,” Hermening said. “I hope you’ll trust me to be our voice in Washington. I want to fight for us during the rough times and cheerlead us through the good ones.”
summary: 11 hours ago WAUSAU — Republican Kevin Hermening formally launched his campaign Thursday for Wisconsin’s open 7th Congressional District seat, entering a crowded GOP primary with a message centered on deep local roots, decades of party involvement and frustration with Washington. “I am prepared to serve from day one.” He cited concerns about federal spending, national debt, border security and economic uncertainty as central motivations for his run.
